source.title: Awareness of errors is reduced by sleep loss

confidence_rationale: The single most load-bearing timescale finding in this pull: it directly dissociates acute total sleep deprivation (TSD, ~one wake episode) from chronic partial sleep restriction (SR, across multiple nights), and finds metacognitive error-awareness drift ONLY in the chronic condition. V3-EXQ-794a's design (30 training episodes, K=1 single-fire sleep) is structurally closer to the acute TSD arm than the chronic SR arm. Confidence held at 0.65: recent, well-designed (combined EEG + behavior, two separate cohorts), but error awareness on a per-trial task is a narrower construct than a continuously-updated precision estimate.
failure_signatures: Acute total sleep deprivation did NOT influence behavioral error awareness, ERN amplitude, or Pe amplitude -- the acute-deprivation regime structurally closest to V3-EXQ-794a's single-episode design showed NO measurable metacognitive drift on this task.

Chronic sleep RESTRICTION (repeated nights of partial sleep loss) DID reduce behavioral error awareness, increase detection latency, and reduce Pe amplitude -- so the drift SD-076 posits is empirically real, but appears to require accumulated exposure across multiple sleep-wake cycles, not a single wake episode, which bears directly on GOV-FANOUT-1's H2 (insufficient training exposure).

If REE's asymmetric-EMA is meant to model the ACUTE, within-episode regime, this paper predicts it should show little to no drift; if it is meant to model the CHRONIC, across-cycles regime, the driver's K=1 single-fire, 30-episode design may simply not accumulate enough exposure to express it -- directly informing whether the fanout's H2 (exposure) or H3 (wrong mechanism) is the better explanation for V3-EXQ-794a's small effect.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Using the Error Awareness Task with combined behavioral and EEG (ERN, Pe) measures across two separate studies, acute total sleep deprivation (14 participants) did not reduce behavioral error awareness or its neural correlates, whereas chronic sleep restriction (27 participants, multiple nights) did reduce behavioral error awareness, slowed error detection, and reduced Pe amplitude.
mapping.ree_translation: REE reads this as the clearest available timescale evidence bearing on GOV-FANOUT-1's H2 (insufficient training exposure) versus H3 (wrong mechanism form). If human metacognitive drift specifically requires chronic, multi-cycle sleep restriction rather than a single acute wake episode to become measurable, then V3-EXQ-794a's 30-episode/K=1 single-fire-sleep full behavioural loop is testing the regime where the biology itself predicts a small or absent effect -- which argues for H2 (extend training exposure across more sleep cycles) over H3 (redesign the mechanism), while not eliminating H3 outright.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Error awareness in a two-choice reaction-time task (recognising that a specific response was wrong) is a narrower and more immediate construct than a continuously-updated running-variance precision estimate that persists and accumulates ACROSS trials -- SD-076's construct is closer to a slow-moving summary statistic than a per-trial awareness judgment. The acute-vs-chronic distinction this paper draws is the load-bearing part of the mapping; the specific EEG/behavioral measures are secondary.
mapping.source_context: Two healthy adult human cohorts (14 under total sleep deprivation, 27 under sleep restriction across nights), combined behavioral (Error Awareness Task) and EEG (ERN, Pe) measures, laboratory setting.

confidence_components.notes: Source quality strong: 2024, purpose-built two-study design directly contrasting acute vs chronic sleep loss with converging behavioral+EEG measures. Mapping fidelity moderate: the acute/chronic timescale distinction maps well onto REE's exposure-budget question, but per-trial error awareness is a narrower construct than an accumulating precision estimate. Transfer risk moderate: the dissociation itself is the useful fact, independent of exact construct match.
